title: Awake, My Heart, with Gladness
description: Awake, My Heart, with Gladness in Tonic Solfa: the solfa line by line with the words, staff notation, all 5 verses, and a piano to sing along with.
about: The words are by Paul Gerhardt, first published in 1648. The English translation is by John Kelly (1867). The tune, AUF, AUF, MEIN HERZ MIT FREUDEN, is by Johann Crüger (1648). This version of the melody and the words comes from the Open Hymnal Project.
underlay: A-wake, my heart, with glad-ness, See what_ to-day_ is done; How af-ter gloom and sad-ness, Comes forth_ the glo_-rious Sun. My Sa-vior there_ was laid Where our bed must_ be made When to_ the realms_ of light Our spi_-rit wings_ its flight.

lines: Where our bed must be made
When to the realms of light
They in the grave did sink Him,
To Christ must he give o'er,
Must yield his feet and hands.
A sight it is to gladden;
And fill the heart with glee,
Shall aught, or take from me
Hell and its prince, the devil,
Of all their pow'rs are shorn;
Now I am safe from evil,
And sin I laugh to scorn.
Grim Death with all his might
